data.name: Houssam
data.gender_notes: Houssam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h-s-m, meaning 'to dedicate, to commit'. In Islamic history, Houssam bin Ali was a devoted companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and an early Muslim warrior. The name Houssam carries the meaning “Dedication, Commitment” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Houssam usually hope their child will grow to embody dedication, commitment and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblematic of faithfulness and devotion to God.
data.etymology: Houssam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dedication, Commitment.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Houssam total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: حسام
in_arabic.meaning: سيف حاد وقاطع للعدو في المعارك
in_arabic.long_meaning: حسام هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه السيف الحاد القاطع، المستخدم في المعارك لقتال الأعداء. يدل على الشجاعة و القوة في مواجهة الصعوبات. ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع لوصف السيف كرمز للقتال في سبيل الله.

in_pashto.name: حسام
in_pashto.meaning: د دښمنو د پرې کولو تېز تور

in_english.meaning: Sharp sword, symbol of bravery and strength
in_english.long_meaning: Houssam is an Arabic name that means 'sharp sword' or 'cutting sword'. It is derived from the Arabic root 'h-s-m', which implies cutting or severing. The name Houssam reflects these qualities and is often chosen for its powerful and positive connotations.

historical_references.reference: Houssam ibn Ali Zarqa, a prominent Sufi mystic and scholar from Andalusia. He is also known as Ibn Houssam Al-Hadrami. He was born in Yemen around 1140 AD and died in Cordoba, Spain in 1198 AD. Houssam was a disciple of Muhyiddin Ibn Arabi and is considered one of the early Sufi masters of the Andalusian tradition. He is known for his influential works on Sufism and Islamic philosophy, including 'Al-Madkhal ila Sufiyya' and 'Al-Ta'arruf li-Madhhab Ahl al-Tasawwuf'.

Al-Houssam ibn Abd Al-Azeez Al-Farooqi, a renowned Islamic scholar and jurist from Tunisia. He was born in the late 18th century AD and died in 1835 AD. Houssam was a member of the Hanafi madhhab and was renowned for his knowledge of Islamic jurisprudence, particularly in the areas of inheritance law and the law of evidence. He authored numerous works on Islamic law and jurisprudence, including 'Al-Mabsut fi Sharh Abi Hanifa' and 'Al-Wajzat fi Sharh Mawsuat Al-Kabir'.
